lines.text: Mordecai sent letters to all the Jews, setting an annual celebration on the fourteenth and fifteenth days of Adar.
Haman, the Agagite, cast the Pur to destroy the Jews, but the king ordered his scheme to fall on his own head.
The days were called Purim, from the word Pur, and the Jews bound themselves to keep them in every generation.
Queen Esther, daughter of Abihail, and Mordecai wrote with full authority, and Mordecai sent letters to the Jews in the 120 provinces.
King Xerxes imposed tribute on the land, and Mordecai was commander of the royal army, written in the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.
